consensus_summary: Fish symbolize people/souls gathered into the kingdom by evangelism or sorted in judgment (fishers of men; dragnet), and/or Christ via the ICHTHYS acrostic, plus secondary links to provision, baptism, and Jonah.
book_summary: Fish symbolize a person in the sea of nations, clean or unclean, gathered and sorted at the harvest by fishers of men drawing the net.
consensus_core_identification: people/souls caught and sorted for the kingdom or judgment (exegetical primary); Christ/ICHTHYS (traditional primary)
book_core_identification: a person in the sea of nations, clean or unclean, gathered and sorted at harvest
rationale: Minimum cores are equivalent: the book’s ‘person... gathered and sorted’ is exactly the consensus exegetical identification from fishers-of-men and the dragnet (good/bad fish), which every response lists as primary or common. Phrasing such as ‘sea of nations’ and ‘clean or unclean’ is immaterial detail drawn from the same texts (Hab 1:14; Matt 13:47-48) and does not replace or contradict the referent. The ICHTHYS/Christ strand is an additional traditional reading that coexists without making the cores unequal.
strongest_objection: The entry omits the ICHTHYS/Christ identification that several consensus responses treat as co-primary or dominant in historical tradition.
